notes:
Summary: Auric is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for mission-critical user-facing chat and high-volume embedding pipelines. Primary ask: clearly defined latency SLOs with measurement alignment (client vs server), guaranteed throughput for reserved GPU pools, and explicit SLA credits for tail misses.

Key technical constraints and preferences:
- Workloads: real-time chat (avg request length 60-120 tokens), streaming responses required for support-agent product; batch embedding jobs (millions of docs) for nightly pipelines; reranking for search result personalization.
- Latency targets requested: p50 < 60ms (server-side token emit), p95 < 200ms, p99 < 500ms for non-streaming short requests; streaming tail expectations: p95 (first-byte) < 150ms, p99 (per-chunk) < 300ms. Want separate SLOs for initial response vs subsequent token latency.
- Measurement alignment: Auric insists on client-side observed timing as source of truth (real user experience) but amenable to hybrid: Redwood metrics + client-side beaconing for dispute resolution. Must define clock skew tolerance, time-sync requirements, and exact RFC for latency measurement (start = client TCP request time OR app-layer sent time).
- Percentile computation: need clarification on sliding-window vs calendar-window percentiles, aggregation (per-region vs global), and whether percentiles are computed on raw samples or bucketed/TDigest approximations. Auric requests monthly reporting and daily alerts on rolling 1h p99.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: want separate pipeline SLAs. Streaming: measure first-byte and per-chunk latency; non-streaming: end-to-end response time. Also want guidance on how partial responses and truncated tokens are accounted for.
- Client vs server timing: require anchored logs for reconciliation: request_id propagation, server timestamps (ingest, model_dispatch, token_emit), and client beacons (first-byte seen, full payload received). Redwood asked about adding a small header for timestamping; Auric will permit if documented and secured.
- Warmup & cache priming: POC must include steady-state measurement after warm-up period (30 min) and also cold-start scenarios. KV cache priming improves p50 but Auric wants worst-case tail guarantees accounted for in SLA.
- Throughput guarantees: reserved GPU configuration targets 200 concurrent chats at 4rps each (sustained) with ability to burst 2x for 5 minutes. Need token/sec guarantees per reserved node and queueing/backpressure semantics defined.
- Scaling behavior: explicit autoscaling boundaries and expected instance spin-up times; what happens when reserved pool saturated — fallback to managed hosted pool or degrade model? Auric prefers graceful fallback to smaller-quantized variant rather than outright reject.
- SLA mechanics: credit formulas for p99 misses, monthly SLO windows, and exclusion allowances (maintenance, force majeure). Procurement pushing for hard credits tied to % of monthly invoice.

POC/Proof points to collect during evaluation:
- 7-day stress run: mix of streaming chats + batch embeddings; record per-request traces with request_id, raw client timestamps, server stages, and model-backend latencies.
- Synthetic latency curves by seq-length (32/64/128/512) and by model variant (fp16/8-bit quant).
- Tail analysis: p99.9 and p99.99 samples flagged for root cause (queueing, kernel stalls, NVLink saturation).
- Throughput certification test to certify X tokens/sec per reserved GPU type (A100-80GB equivalent) with concurrency matrix.
